title: Cartes de visite et confidences  (Business Cards and Confidences)

segments.t: At the agency reception, Herve proudly shows Camille the new business cards he designed. He then drops a surprising revelation, claiming he has figured out the identity of Camille's father. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Ta mère arrive quand?
Elle arrive la semaine prochaine.
Attends, regarde mes cartes de visite.
J'ai passé la nuit à les faire.
C'est pour quand je serai agent junior!
Génial! Cette couleur est plus claire.
Tu as raison, c'est beaucoup mieux.
Je pourrai être ton assistante.
Merci, Camille. Tu es une vraie amie.
Au fait, je sais qui est ton père.
Ah bon? Comment tu sais ça?
C'est évident, voyons!
Tu n'es pas en colère?
Tout le monde a droit à ses secrets.
Je voulais te le dire.
J'adore Christophe Lambert depuis mon enfance!
Tu es incroyable, Hervé!
Let's examine how Herve shares his cards and his funny mistake with Camille.
Ta mère arrive quand?
'When does your mother arrive?' Literally 'Your mother arrives when?'. Hervé puts the question at the end, which is very common in casual conversation. In French, this phrasing is common.
Elle arrive la semaine prochaine.
'She arrives next week.' Literally 'the week next'. Camille puts the describing detail after the main idea, unlike English. You will find this useful in French.
Attends, regarde mes cartes de visite.
'Wait, look at my business cards.' Literally 'cards of visit'. Hervé uses this handy phrase that you'll hear a lot in professional settings. This sounds extremely natural in French.
J'ai passé la nuit à les faire.
'I spent the night making them.' Literally 'I have passed the night to make them'. Hervé describes his late-night effort. In French, this is perfectly fine.
C'est pour quand je serai agent junior!
'It is for when I am a junior agent!' Hervé points out his future goal. In French, you'd use a future action after 'when' here. A standard way to speak in French.
Génial! Cette couleur est plus claire.
'Awesome! This colour is lighter.' Literally 'more light'. Camille notes that the shade is less dark. In French, you will hear this.
Tu as raison, c'est beaucoup mieux.
'You are right, it is much better.' Literally 'You have reason'. Hervé points out that you can say 'have reason' rather than 'are right'. The French say this often.
Je pourrai être ton assistante.
'I will be able to be your assistant.' Camille offers her help. This is built from the future idea of 'can' joined by 'to be'. In French, this is quite common.
Merci, Camille. Tu es une vraie amie.
'Thank you, Camille. You are a true friend.' Hervé uses a cognate for 'true'. It sounds similar in both languages. This is how you say it in French.
Au fait, je sais qui est ton père.
'By the way, I know who your father is.' Literally 'At the fact'. Hervé uses this handy phrase to change the topic. A handy phrase in French.
Ah bon? Comment tu sais ça?
'Really? How do you know that?' Literally 'Oh good?'. Camille acts surprised. You'll hear this expression everywhere. A useful expression in French.
C'est évident, voyons!
'It is obvious, come on!' Literally 'let us see'. Hervé uses this idiom to say 'come on' or 'be reasonable'. This is very typical in French.
Tu n'es pas en colère?
'You are not angry?' Literally 'in anger'. Camille asks this in the negative to check his reaction. A common chunk in French.
Tout le monde a droit à ses secrets.
'Everyone has a right to their secrets.' Literally 'All the world has right'. Hervé uses this handy chunk to mean 'everyone'. You will hear this in French.
Je voulais te le dire.
'I wanted to tell you.' Literally 'I wanted to you it tell'. Hervé puts the target objects right before the action. This is perfectly natural in French.
J'adore Christophe Lambert depuis mon enfance!
'I have loved Christophe Lambert since my childhood!' Unlike English, the action happens in the present because it is still going on now. In French, it works nicely.
Tu es incroyable, Hervé!

'You are incredible, Hervé!' Camille is relieved. You can swap in different names to compliment someone like this. The French use this a lot. Now let's listen to the whole discussion again without stopping.
Ta mère arrive quand?
Elle arrive la semaine prochaine.
Attends, regarde mes cartes de visite.
J'ai passé la nuit à les faire.
C'est pour quand je serai agent junior!
Génial! Cette couleur est plus claire.
Tu as raison, c'est beaucoup mieux.
Je pourrai être ton assistante.
Merci, Camille. Tu es une vraie amie.
Au fait, je sais qui est ton père.
Ah bon? Comment tu sais ça?
C'est évident, voyons!
Tu n'es pas en colère?
Tout le monde a droit à ses secrets.
Je voulais te le dire.
J'adore Christophe Lambert depuis mon enfance!
Tu es incroyable, Hervé!
Herve proudly displays his agency ambition and shares his wild theory about Camille's father. Camille is secretly relieved that her true parentage remains safe. See you next time!
À plus tard, Camille!
